The user then asked about specific policies: Accenture caregiver return-to-work, Goldman Sachs unconscious-bias training, Microsoft and P&G mentorship, Goldman Sachs and Accenture parental leave, and Microsoft and P&G flexible work.

The assistant provided detailed claims about programs, eligibility, leave duration, outcomes, training requirements, mentorship structures, and flexible options. These details may be inaccurate, outdated, conflated, or unsupported and must not be repeated as verified facts without checking authoritative, current sources, ideally official company pages and recent reports. This is especially important for prior claims such as Accenture’s alleged 16-week/12-month-eligibility caregiver program and reported return/confidence outcomes; Goldman Sachs’ alleged global 20-week leave and mandatory bias training; Accenture’s alleged global 22-week leave and concierge service; Microsoft LEAP eligibility and cadence; P&G Women’s Network membership; and universal availability of compressed weeks, job sharing, or ROWE at those companies. Policies often vary by country, worker classification, tenure, role, business unit, and leave type.

Do not treat them as verified facts; if the topic continues, ask the user for the actual roles and leadership structure rather than repeating invented details.
